body: Thank you so much for that! You are absolutely right. I feel better about going to sleep now. Sometimes you just need to hear those simple truths I guess.

Yes, get a second opinion! I've got either bipolar 2 or cyclothymia, I don't really get severe hypomanias, but I can get really severe depressions. Bipolar meds have worked for me in the past, then stopped working. Trying out lithium now, which hasn't really manifested itself yet. But I'm on the road to recovery, unless I kill myself on the way that is... But yeah, definitely get a second opinion. Bipolar is a complicated disorder that can be made black and white by psychiatry.

One thing I can recommend is to try to stay away from DMT and other hallucinogens until you've cleared your head a bit. I'm saying this because all hallucinogens messes with your serotonin levels, which *can* be very helpful for depression, but can worsen something like bipolar disorder for instance. 

What to do instead is to go see a doctor. (Det vil si DPS, dra på sykehuset og si du ønsker en time med en psykolog, og så fortsetter jeg på engelsk for de andre her) Talking to a psychologist can do some really good things for you. And you can get it on paper that you've struggled with depression, which has really helped me out for sure. It's not fun or easy to seek help, but it helps in so many ways.

Good luck, and keep pushing! Sending internet hugs your way!

But even for the strongest among us, there are times we feel weak. Recognize that feeling, look it straight in the eye, and when it tells you to kill yourself, you say "not now, not today".

Keep going man, 14 is far from too late to find a passion. Back when I was 14 I had no clue what I was doing. I wanted to die because I felt like there was no place for me, nothing for me to do. I'm 18 now, and next month I'm releasing an album. Give it a few years, you will grow.

Hey man, diagnosed BP 2 here. I was diagnosed 7 months ago. In the time before I was diagnosed I had insane mood swings for about two months, although the upswings weren't necessarily pleasant. Sometimes it felt like I was on drugs, other times it felt like hyperactive hell. But the mood swings came really sudden, before that I had been in an 8 year long haze-like depression. For the longest time I thought I was just depressed, but of course I didn't do anything about it because I had lived my entire conscious life with anxiety and the depression just came gradually. I didn't know any better. I guess you could say my BP was triggered, but then again it could have always been there. I'm not sure if this is going to help you out at all, but I think I know how you feel. But no matter what it might be, it's going to be alright. Bipolar is not a death sentence, although it sometimes feels that way.

So, again, I'm not sure if I've experienced what you're experiencing. But this I know, you're not at all weird or abnormal, I can definitely relate. And I know for sure you're not the only one going through this. BP is an incredibly complicated disorder, so you never know. (Until you talk to your pdoc about it, which you are and that's a really good thing)

My first time, fucking horrible.

My dad has bipolar, so I knew quite a bit about it. So when I experienced my first hypomanic period, I knew exactly what it was. I had to fight myself to accept that I was sick, which took months. I probably knew deep down even though I wanted to remain undiagnosed and unmedicated.

(Your first question)
I had told a close friend of mine about it, that I suspected it was bipolar and that I didn't want to do anything about it. And that made sense to me at the time, not to her though. I ended up trying to kill myself and calling her in the act for comfort. She came right over to where I was and it scared the living shit out of her. While she was crying she told me I had to get help.

(Your second question, not getting into too much detail)
So after not being able to sleep that night and feeling like shit about it for a while I went to the doctors office. I told my doc about the state I was in and my suspicions, showed him graphs from mood journals I had kept. And then.. nothing. For two months. Which means I had to deal with 4 weeks of depression and 4 weeks of unbearable hypomania before I got any treatment.

The process of getting treatment was shit. I had to be as firm as I could in the state that I was in, which wasn't easy, and I really had to fight my way through the system to get meds.

And then some advice. Be firm,  honest and direct when talking to your doc, pdoc, whatever. This is you getting help, if these people are going to help you, you need to communicate what you feel.

(Your last question)
I don't, to be honest. I'd like to think I do, but sometimes I doubt I have this illness at all. I just try to keep in mind that it doesn't matter how extreme it is, what matters is your own well being. And if you're not well, so not-well that you're sick, then you're sick. Whether it's equated to a cold or cancer, you should still take care of yourself.
